We need to determine appropriate crime(s) based on facts. Facts: Breakfast shop owner mistakenly put a bag of淡黄色颗粒物质 (likely sodium nitrite) into sugar bowl, causing poisoning. 13 people ate, 1 died. This is a case of food poisoning leading to death. In Chinese criminal law, this would be "非法投放有毒有害食品致人死亡" maybe "投放有毒有害食品罪" (罪名: 投放有毒有害食品罪). The specific crime is "非法投放有毒有害食品罪" (Article 144 of Criminal Law). Also possibly "过失致人死亡" if it was negligence, but the facts say "误当作白糖倒入糖盆内" - mistaken, not intentional. The prosecution may charge "过失致人死亡" (negligent homicide) or "投放有毒有害食品罪" which requires intent to poison? The law: Article 144: "生产、销售有毒、有害食品，致人中毒死亡的，处七年以上有期徒刑或者无期徒刑" etc. But here it's not production/sale, but adding to food. Could be "非法投放有毒有害食品罪". The key is whether there is intent. The facts say "误当作是白糖倒入糖盆内" - accidental. So maybe "过失致人死亡" (negligent homicide). However Chinese criminal law also has "以危险方法危害公共安全罪" maybe not. The typical classification for food poisoning accidents is "过失致人死亡" if no intent. The examples: earlier they had "重大责任事故" for workplace accidents. For fire they used "失火". For negligence causing death they used "过失致人死亡;破坏生产经营". So here we have poisoning due to negligence. So likely "过失致人死亡". Also maybe "非法投放有毒有害食品罪" if they consider it as "投放有毒有害食品". The rule: only use specific crime if facts mention that. The facts mention "亚硝酸盐中毒". Not mention "投放有毒有害食品罪". So we should not assume that. Use "过失致人死亡". Also maybe "食品安全犯罪"? But not in list. So answer: [罪名]过失致人死亡<eoa>
